newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Dept to issue experimental CPI April 10.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Dept to issue experimental CPI April 10.

text.p: The Labor Department said Monday that on April 10 it will begin regular publication of an experimental index on Consumer Prices.
The new index uses a geometric mean instead of the arithmetic mean formula to calculate price changes at the basic level of detail.
The experimental CPI gauge -- called CPI-U-XG -- was produced by the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics to examine ways to make regular monthly CPI a more accurate measure of price change.

Data released April 10 will show monthly price changes for Dec 1990-Feb 1997. They will include all items; the seven broad components of food, housing, apparel, transportation, medical care, entertainment, and other goods and services; and the special indexes for food and energy, and all items less food and energy.
The department will brief reporters and take questions at 0930 hrs EDT (1330 GMT) on April 10.
On April 15, the department will issue the next monthly report on regular CPI data for March.
